aamisc1.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: Outside classes I to IV, which two drugs make up the antiarrhythmic "others" group?
opts: Amiodarone and sotalol are class III drugs (sotalol adds class II activity); the others are adenosine and digitalis.
Esmolol is a class II beta blocker and verapamil a class IV calcium channel blocker; the others are adenosine and digitalis.
Lidocaine is class IB and flecainide class IC, both sodium channel blockers; the others are adenosine and digitalis.
Correct. The classification lists adenosine and digitalis (digoxin) as the others, outside classes I to IV.

aamisc1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: What should a patient be warned about just before receiving adenosine?
opts: The heart may stop for a few seconds
Correct. Adenosine may stop the heart for 2 to 3 seconds, and flushing, shortness of breath and chest burning can follow.
Blue-gray skin with photosensitivity is an amiodarone effect over time; adenosine may stop the heart for seconds.
The ears may ring with dizziness
Tinnitus, dizziness and blurred vision are quinidine's cinchonism; adenosine may stop the heart for seconds.
The hands may shake with blurred vision
Blurred vision and tremor are listed for flecainide; adenosine may stop the heart for a few seconds.

aamisc1.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: Which arrhythmia is the main listed indication for adenosine?
opts: Correct. Adenosine is listed for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.
Ventricular tachycardia resistant to other drugs is an amiodarone indication; adenosine is for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.
Ventricular fibrillation is listed for lidocaine and amiodarone; adenosine is for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.
Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate; adenosine is for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.

aamisc1.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: Which adverse effect occurs in about one in five patients given adenosine?
opts: Nystagmus is the early sign of lidocaine toxicity; the common adenosine effect is flushing.
Thrombocytopenia is listed for quinidine and flecainide; the common adenosine effect is flushing.
Corneal deposits are an amiodarone toxicity of long-term use; the common adenosine effect is flushing.
Correct. Flushing occurs in about 20% of patients given adenosine, with shortness of breath and chest burning also listed.

aamisc1.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: Which agent is given intravenously for torsades de pointes?
opts: Dofetilide causes torsades de pointes (with marked QT prolongation) rather than treating it; magnesium sulfate treats it.
Correct. Intravenous magnesium sulfate is the listed treatment for torsades de pointes.
Amiodarone prolongs repolarization as a class III drug; the listed treatment for torsades de pointes is magnesium sulfate.
Procainamide lists torsades de pointes among its adverse effects; the listed treatment for torsades is magnesium sulfate.

aamisc1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: What is digoxin's primary molecular action?
opts: Activating atrial potassium channels is adenosine's action; digoxin inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase.
Correct. Digoxin (digitalis) inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase, slows atrioventricular conduction and can induce heart block.
Blocking potassium channels is the class III mechanism; digoxin inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase.
Beta-1 receptor blockade is the class II mechanism of metoprolol; digoxin inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase.

aamisc1.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: Which drugs are listed to avoid alongside digoxin?
opts: Correct. Calcium blockers and beta blockers are listed to avoid with digoxin; they add to its slowing of atrioventricular conduction.
Opioids such as codeine and morphine
Codeine and morphine are the opioids affected by quinidine's cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibition; digoxin is to be avoided with calcium blockers and beta blockers.
Warfarin is a drug whose level amiodarone raises; digoxin is to be avoided with calcium blockers and beta blockers.
Sodium channel blockers such as lidocaine
Lidocaine is the intravenous class IB sodium channel blocker; digoxin is to be avoided with calcium blockers and beta blockers.

aamisc1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: Which central nervous system effects are listed for digoxin toxicity?
opts: Neuropathy, muscle weakness and ataxia belong to amiodarone; digoxin causes confusion and visual disturbances.
Tinnitus, dizziness and blurred vision are quinidine's cinchonism; digoxin causes confusion and visual disturbances.
Correct. Digoxin's central nervous system toxicity includes confusion, delirium, headache, seizures and visual disturbances.
Nystagmus and muscle twitches belong to lidocaine's toxicity; digoxin causes confusion and visual disturbances.

aamisc1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc1.q: Which antiarrhythmic may stop the heart for 2 to 3 seconds?
opts: Esmolol is the intravenous, short-acting beta blocker; the drug that may stop the heart for seconds is adenosine.
Digoxin slows atrioventricular conduction and can induce heart block, but the brief pause is adenosine's.
Correct. Adenosine decreases conduction velocity and may stop the heart for 2 to 3 seconds; its half-life is about 10 seconds.
Magnesium sulfate treats torsades de pointes and can cause bradycardia; the brief pause is adenosine's.

aamisc2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: Which serious toxicity is listed for magnesium sulfate?
opts: Correct. Magnesium sulfate's listed toxicities are bradycardia, flushing, headache and respiratory paralysis.
Pulmonary fibrosis (potentially fatal) is amiodarone's lung toxicity; magnesium sulfate can cause respiratory paralysis.
Bronchospasm is listed for propranolol, sotalol and the class IC drugs; magnesium sulfate can cause respiratory paralysis.
Pneumonitis is amiodarone's lung toxicity; magnesium sulfate can cause respiratory paralysis.

aamisc2.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: Which heart rate effect is listed for magnesium sulfate?
opts: Magnesium sulfate slows rather than speeds the heart; bradycardia is on its toxicity list.
Torsades de pointes is what magnesium sulfate treats, not a toxicity of it; bradycardia is on its list.
Increased atrioventricular conduction is listed for lidocaine; magnesium sulfate's heart rate effect is bradycardia.
Correct. Bradycardia is on magnesium sulfate's toxicity list, with flushing, headache and respiratory paralysis.

aamisc2.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: Why is adenosine's effect so brief?
opts: It is cleared unchanged by the kidneys
Elimination unchanged by the kidneys describes dofetilide; adenosine's effect is brief because of its 10-second half-life.
Correct. Adenosine's half-life is about 10 seconds, so the pause it causes is brief.
Acetylation describes procainamide and its active metabolite; adenosine's effect is brief because of its 10-second half-life.
Extensive first-pass metabolism is why lidocaine is given intravenously; adenosine's effect is brief because of its half-life.

aamisc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: What does digoxin do to autonomic tone on the heart?
opts: Correct. Digoxin indirectly increases parasympathetic tone and decreases sympathetic tone, slowing atrioventricular conduction.
This reverses both directions; digoxin indirectly raises parasympathetic tone and lowers sympathetic tone.
Digoxin lowers sympathetic tone rather than raising it, while it indirectly raises parasympathetic tone.
Digoxin raises parasympathetic tone rather than lowering it, while it lowers sympathetic tone.

aamisc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: What does adenosine do to the membrane potential of atrial and nodal cells?
opts: Correct. Adenosine hyperpolarizes the cells, which decreases conduction velocity and automaticity.
Depolarizing the cells would make firing easier; adenosine hyperpolarizes them and slows conduction.
Slowing the phase 0 upstroke is the class IA and IC sodium channel effect; adenosine hyperpolarizes the cells.
Delaying phase 3 is the class III effect; adenosine hyperpolarizes the cells.

aamisc2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: Anorexia, nausea and vomiting with delirium and visual disturbances point to toxicity from which drug?
opts: Dofetilide's listed adverse effects are torsades de pointes and marked QT prolongation; this gastrointestinal and visual picture is digoxin's.
ruled out by a stated finding
Esmolol is the intravenous, short-acting beta blocker, with no gastrointestinal or visual toxicity listed; this picture is digoxin's.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Digoxin toxicity lists nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and anorexia with confusion, delirium, headache, seizures and visual disturbances.
Magnesium sulfate's listed effects are bradycardia, flushing, headache and respiratory paralysis; this picture is digoxin's.
ruled out by a stated finding

aamisc2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: Which set of adverse effects is listed for adenosine?
opts: Bradycardia, flushing, headache and respiratory paralysis are listed for magnesium sulfate; adenosine adds dyspnea and chest burning.
Gastrointestinal upset, confusion and visual disturbances are digoxin toxicity; adenosine causes flushing, dyspnea and chest burning.
Tinnitus, dizziness and blurred vision are quinidine's cinchonism; adenosine causes flushing, dyspnea and chest burning.
Flushing, shortness of breath, chest burning
Correct. Adenosine's listed toxicities are flushing (20%), shortness of breath and burning in the chest.

aamisc2.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: In atrial flutter or fibrillation, what is digoxin used to do?
opts: Normal rhythm in atrial fibrillation is dofetilide's listed indication; digoxin slows the ventricular rate.
Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate; digoxin slows the ventricular rate.
Correct. Digoxin is listed to slow the ventricular rate, inducing a degree of heart block in atrial flutter and fibrillation.
Digoxin slows atrioventricular conduction and can induce heart block, which is how it slows the ventricular rate.

aamisc2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aamisc2.q: How does adenosine act on potassium channels in the atria?
opts: Blocking potassium channels is the class III mechanism, which prolongs repolarization; adenosine activates them.
Correct. Adenosine activates potassium channels in the atria and blocks calcium channels, which hyperpolarizes the cells.
Slow recovery of channels describes class IC sodium channel block; adenosine activates atrial potassium channels.
Adenosine's action starts at these channels: it activates atrial potassium channels and blocks calcium channels.
